ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening of all UBOs, managers, and authorized signatories against the EU Consolidated Sanctions List, the UN Security Council Consolidated List, the Luxembourg national assets-freezing measures, and OFAC SDN list as a prudent bank-accepted standard. Mandatory enhanced due diligence for politically exposed persons (PEPs), verification of beneficial ownership through the 25% ownership and control threshold, and ongoing transaction monitoring under the amended Law of 12 November 2004.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), available at www.lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must be available, distinguishable from existing RCS registrations, and rendered in Latin script. French, German, and Luxembourgish are the administrative languages. Chinese characters are not accepted as the legal company name in the RCS; a Latin-script transliteration is required and the legal form suffix 'SARL' must be included. Foreign names may be added as a secondary trade name after incorporation.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a rejection notice from the RCS, the applicant or the notary may resubmit a corrected name. If the refusal is maintained, the applicant may file a written administrative complaint with the Luxembourg Business Registers. If unresolved, judicial recourse lies before the Commercial Chamber of the Luxembourg District Court (Tribunal d'arrondissement) through a Luxembourg-qualified lawyer. An appeal must be brought within the statutory time limits provided by Luxembourg procedural law; name reservation is not automatically renewable after expiry.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual mailbox is not permitted as the registered office of a Luxembourg SARL. The registered office must be a physical address in Luxembourg where the company's administration and statutory records are effectively maintained. Commercial domiciliation by an approved corporate domiciliation service provider with physical Luxembourg premises is permissible for a non-regulated commercial 3D animation company, provided the domiciliation agent is duly compliant with the Law of 31 May 1999.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low to moderate (estimated 10-25%). Unannounced physical inspections are rare for a non-regulated CGI/animation production company, but may occur where the registered office is a commercial domiciliation service and AML/CFT authorities audit the service provider's compliance.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended – Articles 710 to 766 (SARL); Law of 19 December 2002 on the Trade and Companies Register and on the accounting records and annual accounts of undertakings, as amended
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial deed of incorporation (acte de constitution) and coordinated articles of association (statuts coordonnés), published in the Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital EUR 12,000 fully subscribed and fully paid up at incorporation; cash contributions deposited into a blocked account in the name of the company in formation, and contributions in kind fully paid up and certified by the notary
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) the initial share capital of EUR 12,000 is approved, fully subscribed and paid up in cash as stated in the notarial deed of incorporation; (2) the shares are allotted to the subscribers in accordance with the articles of association; (3) the registered office is fixed at [Address], Luxembourg City, Grand Duchy of Luxembourg, and the managers are instructed to execute the office lease and to register the seat with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register; (4) [Name] and [Name] are appointed as managers (gérants), each with sole signature authority; and (5) the managers are authorized to publish the incorporation in the RESA and to complete tax, social security and commercial formalities necessary for the company's operations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate name availability check and pre-registration preparation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) online portal (RCS Luxembourg)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct an online name search on lbr.lu to confirm the proposed corporate name is available and not identical or confusingly similar to existing registered names. Obtain a non-objection reference if the name is approved after preliminary screening; prepare the draft articles of association and capital evidence for the notary.
required_dossiers: Identification documents of shareholders and managers
Certificate of blocked capital account or bank confirmation of deposit
Proof of powers for corporate shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for similarity, select a new name and re-submit the availability check; the subsequent notarial deed will use the accepted name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the notarial deed of incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary (Notaire) authorized by the Ministry of Justice
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the incorporation ceremony before a Luxembourg notary. The notary verifies the subscribers' identities and capacity, reads the articles of association, obtains the capital subscription and payment acknowledgement, and authenticates the deed. The notary also prepares the coordination act of the articles for RCS filing.
required_dossiers: Passport or national identity card of each shareholder in formation
Corporate documents and authorization of corporate shareholders (if any)
Proof of payment of the share capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies a defect in corporate capacity or capital proof, the incorporation is postponed until the document is cured; if the deed contains a correcting point, a rectification deed or additional authenticated act will be executed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary electronically files the incorporation dossier and the coordination act with the RCS. The RCS verifies statutory compliance, records the company, and allocates the Luxembourg company registration number (RCS number). After registration, the company obtains legal personality.
required_dossiers: Coordination act of the articles of association
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS returns a query, the notary supplies the missing legalization or clarification and re-files the dossier. If the query concerns the corporate name, a corrective resolution and amending articles are executed and re-filed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the RESA and issue of the RCS extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The RCS arranges publication of a notice of incorporation in RESA, including the company's corporate form, capital, registered office, managers, and purpose. After publication, obtain the certified RCS extract and company registration certificate as conclusive evidence of formation.
required_dossiers: Power of attorney for extract collection
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If publication is delayed, contact LBR support with the filing reference; any errors in the published notice are corrected by a RCS rectification filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, VAT, and social security registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD), Administration de l'Enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA (AED), Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the RCS extract, register the company for corporate income tax and municipal business tax with ACD, for Luxembourg VAT with AED, and for social security of the managers and employees with CCSS. Obtain the Luxembourg tax identification number and VAT number; conclude any employer and workplace declarations.
required_dossiers: RCS extract and certificate of incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax or social security registration is queried, correct the registration form and submit supplementary documents via MyGuichet; late VAT registration may result in a request to regularize the effective-start-date.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable – no sectoral industrial establishment licence required for commercial CGI, VFX and 3D animation production services under Luxembourg law
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No operating licence applicable; the company may rely on its RCS registration and general business compliance for unregulated service activities

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'Environnement / Environmental Protection Agency
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – office-based CGI/animation production is not listed in the categories requiring a full EIA or environmental impact study under the Law of 15 May 2018 on environmental impact assessment
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater, VOC or stack emission thresholds apply. General hygiene and municipal wastewater discharge standards apply for sanitary wastewater; e-waste from IT equipment must be managed in accordance with the Law on waste management and WEEE collection obligations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification of the registered office/workplace by the competent municipal authority and the Grand-Ducal Fire and Rescue Corps if required; structural load and premises clearance certificate from the landlord/municipality; occupational health and safety review under the Labour Code before opening the office premises.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct taxes; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT and registration duties; central e-portal MyGuichet.lu / Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Upon notarial incorporation of the SARL, the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) assigns the RCS registration number and the business/tax identification number (numéro d'immatriculation), which is used by ACD for direct tax filings. The SARL must then apply for a Luxembourg VAT identification number (LU + numeric ID) with AEDT through MyGuichet.lu/eDesk using the standard VAT registration procedure. A non-resident foreign entity making taxable supplies in Luxembourg must register directly with AEDT; where the entity is established outside the EU, a Luxembourg tax representative is generally required. The application must state the business activity, shareholders and beneficial owners, place of establishment, and expected turnover. VAT registration is required before taxable supplies begin or as soon as the annual turnover threshold is exceeded.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; resident SARL is treated as a fully taxable separate person subject to Luxembourg corporate income tax, municipal business tax, net wealth tax and VAT; no fiscal transparency or pass-through eligibility.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box and no transparent entity election. A Luxembourg SARL may elect fiscal unity (intégration fiscale) under Art. 164bis LIR for corporate income tax and municipal business tax purposes, and VAT grouping (assujetti unique) under Art. 60 LTV for Luxembourg VAT consolidation. It may also elect the optional 80% IP-box deduction for qualifying IP income under Art. 50bis LIR. Hybrid mismatch rules under ATAD apply mandatorily and override bilateral treatment; no elective hybrid-mismatch election is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, TVA) under the amended Loi TVA of 12 February 1979 and EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual turnover threshold for the Luxembourg small-business VAT franchise; no threshold for a resident SARL making taxable supplies, intra-Community acquisitions or imports; registration is required before taxable supplies begin and is obligatory when the threshold is exceeded. Non-resident suppliers with taxable supplies in Luxembourg may be required to register regardless of turnover, subject to OSS/reverse-charge exceptions.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance or mandatory digital stamping for B2B invoicing in Luxembourg. Invoices issued for VAT purposes must satisfy EU invoicing rules under Art. 5 LTV; B2G e-invoicing to Luxembourg public authorities must be transmitted via compliant PEPPOL formats where required. VAT returns are filed periodically (usually monthly or quarterly) through the AEDT e-space; no API-based real-time clearance is currently imposed on commercial animation/VFX service providers.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported physically outside the EU qualify for 0% VAT if the SARL retains proof of removal from EU territory, including customs export declaration, transport and payment evidence. Intra-EU B2B supplies and B2B services supplied to customers established outside Luxembourg are subject to place-of-supply rules and do not attract Luxembourg VAT where the customer is a taxable person; exports of tangible animation assets, such as master files on storage media, qualify for zero-rating on physical export. Services to non-EU B2B customers and cross-border B2B services to EU customers are generally not subject to Luxembourg VAT, provided the taxable status and establishment evidence is contemporaneous.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD / EBL) for physical exports
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill or CMR transport document
Commercial invoice and export contract (sales order / service agreement)
Proof of foreign customer establishment and taxable status, including the customer's VAT registration number or foreign tax identification
Inward remittance certificate or bank wire confirmation for the export consideration
Production/service delivery records and technical documentation evidencing the 3D animation services supplied
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEDT may claw back zero-rated VAT if the documentary bundle is incomplete or the supplier cannot substantiate physical export or the foreign business destination of the services. The disputed VAT becomes payable with default interest, and monetary fines may be imposed; intentional fraud may lead to criminal fines and imprisonment. Luxembourg's VAT assessment period is normally five years, extended to ten years in fraud cases, so export zero-rating files should be retained for at least that full period.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque Centrale du Luxembourg (BCL); monetary policy competence is vested exclusively in the European Central Bank (ECB) within the Eurosystem. Prudential and AML supervision of banks and non-bank payment institutions is exercised by the CSSF (Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier), with the BCL performing oversight of payment, clearing and settlement systems and compiling mandatory balance-of-payments (BOP) statistics.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg is a euro-area member with EUR as sole legal tender. There is no exchange control law and no restriction on inward or outward transfer of funds for current or capital account transactions, as guaranteed by Articles 63 and 64 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union. Profit remittance is unblocked: interest and royalties incur zero Luxembourg withholding tax; dividend withholding tax is 15% domestically, 0% for EU/EEA corporate shareholders under the Parent-Subsidiary Directive (participation of at least 10% held for 12 months), and reduced treaty rates apply otherwise. Capital contribution, invoiced service payments, loan repayments and dividend distributions may all be effected without prior administrative authorization. Remaining formalities are limited to EU financial sanctions screening (e.g., EU Regulation 833/2014 as amended), suspicious transaction reporting, CRS/FATCA reporting, and BCL BOP statistical declarations for resident transactions exceeding EUR 50,000 per transaction or aggregated thresholds.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Non-applicable in the euro area. Luxembourg imposes no statutory surrender, repatriation or conversion requirement on export proceeds; the SARL may retain foreign currency receivables (e.g., USD, GBP) indefinitely in any bank or non-bank payment account. Only statistical obligations apply: the resident company must report inward and outward service trade settlements to the BCL under the Luxembourg BOP reporting framework, and the intermediary bank generally files the transaction-level declaration. The 3D animation studio should maintain a VAT-compliant invoice trail for each export service to satisfy both BOP classification (EBOPS service category) and Luxembourg VAT rules governing B2B services place of supply.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility, only as an operational disbursement augmentation layer; not viable for statutory capital. Wise B2B (Wise Europe S.A./Wise Payments Ltd) is an EEA/UK e-money institution passported into Luxembourg, not a Luxembourg credit institution; it can open current-account style multi-currency accounts and issue IBANs, and is legally permitted to provide payment services to an LU SARL under the revised Payment Services Directive (PSD2) and the E-Money Directive. Legal constraints: (1) the SARL's société en formation cannot use an EMI for the capital subscription because the notarized deed must be supported by a bank attestation bancaire issued by a credit institution, not an EMI; (2) EMI balances are e-money claims, not deposits, and are not covered by the Luxembourg deposit guarantee scheme (FGDL — Fonds de Garantie Dépôts Luxembourg); (3) EMIs may not grant credit or overdrafts; (4) treasury policy should cap EMI balances at operational day-to-day levels (e.g., below EUR 50,000) and route client receipts above that threshold to a Tier-1 prudential bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: First-time account opening for a non-resident-owned SARL in the 3D animation sector typically requires one managing director and each ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) to attend an in-person interview at the bank or before a Luxembourg notary; however, under the Law of 25 March 2020 on video identification, CSSF-regulated banks may complete remote KYC via audited video-identification procedures combined with LuxTrust/electronic signatures and certified true-copy documentation. In practice, private and mid-corporate banks still mandate a physical visit or a notarized civil-law power of attorney for the first account opening where the UBO is a foreign individual or a non-resident holding company. A viable alternative is a Luxembourg corporate services provider holding a CSSF-licensed professional-client (PFS) status acting as bank introduction agent, preserving remote processing while satisfying the KYC interview requirement

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: non-resident UBO and opaque multi-jurisdictional holding chain above the LU SARL, which may trigger enhanced due diligence under CSSF Regulation 12-02 and the Law of 12 November 2004 on AML/CFT.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized articles of association and amendments; current extract from the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS); Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE) extract showing the ultimate natural persons; full organizational chart with ownership percentages; certified passports and proof of residential address for all UBOs and directors; clean criminal record extracts; CVs or professional references confirming the bona fides of the 3D animation founders.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: high-volume cross-border service invoicing to studios and platform clients in multiple jurisdictions (US, UK, Canada, France) with disproportionately high gross margins typical of capital-light CGI production.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed production and licensing agreements (MSA and Statements of Work) itemizing the 3D animation and VFX scope; VAT-compliant invoices showing Luxembourg VAT identification, invoice number, service description referencing ISIC 5911, and payment terms; project deliverables evidence (pre-vis, render logs, WIP screen captures, delivery receipts); time and cost accounting records (hourly breakdowns, subcontract agreements with render-farm providers); audited or accountant-reviewed financial statements confirming revenue recognition under IFRS 15.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: reliance on Wise B2B and other non-bank EMIs for incoming client funds, which banks treat as potential layering or unverified third-party funding.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board-approved Treasury and Payment Rails Memorandum specifying that EMI accounts are used only for inbound client payments and operational disbursements below EUR 50,000; the official payment institution license and passporting evidence of the EMI; six months of EMI transaction statements reconciled against qualified invoices; confirmation letter from the EMI that no anonymized crypto or third-party funds pass through the account; corridor analysis demonstrating that all counterparties are listed corporate clients in the production contract register.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: subscription of the statutory share capital from a foreign holding company or individual without traceable source-of-wealth documentation, potentially triggering refusal of the bank attestation bancaire.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Source-of-funds file for the capital contribution: bank statements of the transferring account for the prior 12 months; sale-and-purchase agreements or dividend resolutions explaining the origin of the funds; tax returns or wealth declarations of the contributing UBO; tax identification numbers of all contributors; a notarized statement of contribution covering compliance with the recovered-funds provisions of the Luxembourg AML law; confirmation that the funds are immobilized on a blocked capital account until the RCS registration of the SARL.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: disbursements to freelance artists, VFX subcontractors and software/SaaS providers in high-risk or sanctioned-adjacent jurisdictions (or use of virtual asset service providers for payroll).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete subcontract register with VAT numbers and legal entity identifiers of each freelancer; contractual agreements with fixed-fee or milestone payment terms; invoice evidence for each outbound payment; proof that payments are made exclusively to named bank accounts matching the supplier contract; a compliance policy memorandum prohibiting cryptocurrency payments and payments to sanctioned jurisdiction entities; periodic sanctions screening reports from a reputable screening tool; confirmation that the SARL maintains an economic-substance file (registered office, board meetings, personnel, project management activity in Luxembourg).

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol for share capital injection into the LU SARL: (1) the founding UBO or parent company transfers EUR into the blocked capital subscription account opened at an approved Luxembourg credit institution under the SARL's corporate name 'LU SARL(société en formation)', referencing field 70 of the SWIFT MT103, e.g., 'CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION / SARL IN FORMATION / NOMINATIVE LIST OF SUBSCRIBERS' or, for SEPA payments, structured remittance information; (2) the notary requests the bank attestation certifying that the minimum statutory capital of EUR 12,000 (fully paid) is held and blocked until notarization; (3) after notarization, the bank statement of the blocked account must reflect release of funds to the free operational account; (4) for statutory formalities, include the RCS reservation number and the identity of each subscriber; (5) foreign-currency capital contributions (e.g., USD) must be converted to EUR at the ECB reference rate and any conversion loss must be topped up to preserve the minimum capital; (6) the bank and BCL treat the injection as a direct investment inflow to Luxembourg and require BOP statistical reporting under the Luxembourg investor-in-liabilities category; (7) sanctions screening applies to the ordering customer, intermediary banks and the UBO, so the origin of funds documentation must be provided before credit is given.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rail for trade disbursements of on-going 3D animation projects is the SWIFT MT103 / MT202 COV message via the bank's corporate e-banking platform, used for all non-EUR and extra-EEA settlements (e.g., paying US studio partners and UK freelancers), with mandatory field 70 structured remittance referencing the qualified invoice, P.O. number and service description. For EUR payments inside the SEPA zone, the rail is the SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) with a maximum execution time of one business day and no practical value cap, processed through T2 (RTGS) or EURO1/STEP2 batch systems for same-day high-value credits. The bank should be instructed to use the ISO 20022 pain.001 message with the purpose code TXND/SUPP for service fees, so that the beneficiary's bank applies the correct EBOPS classification. For high-value disbursements above EUR 1 million, T2 direct participation (via the bank as member) provides finality; for ordinary VAT and payroll runs, SEPA Direct Debit (SDD) is available. Commercial Letters of Credit (L/C) are not a standard instrument for CGI/VFX service trade; they should be avoided and replaced by MT103 documentary transfers with warranties against non-delivery, because services are intangible and bank-confirmed L/Cs create unnecessary discrepancies and eligibility risk. The SARL should maintain at least two beneficiary banks and one Wise B2B backup to ensure treasury resilience when intra-EU correspondent lines fail; cross-border outgoing wires should be batched before 11:00 CET to meet Luxembourg cut-off for same-day value.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain vanilla deliverable FX forwards traded with an EEA-licensed credit institution under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement (or Luxembourg local form) — primarily EUR/USD and EUR/GBP to lock future client and international distribution revenues.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for currencies without full convertibility, permitted only where the underlying exposure is a confirmed production contract (e.g., remote visualization services for customers in restricted countries), documented so that the NDF settles against the reference rate without a deliverable leg.

FX swaps for short-term liquidity rolling of USD receivables into EUR operational cash, executed under the same ISDA/CSA framework and subject to the SARL treasury policy prohibiting speculative positions.

Vanilla FX options and zero-premium collars to protect annual USD revenue budgets without sacrificing upside, allowable as hedge-only instruments under the Luxembourg company law and IFRS 9 hedge accounting rules if the hedge relationship is formally documented.

Cross-currency swaps for long-term financing or intercompany loans denominated in USD or GBP with mirror accounting, permitted under EU EMIR rules with CCP clearing threshold monitoring and confirmation/trade reporting obligations if volume thresholds are exceeded.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: E-filing of the statutory annual accounts (comptes annuels) as approved by shareholders
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (LBR RCSL)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months after the balance-sheet date (e.g., 31 July for a calendar-year SARL); shareholders must approve the accounts within 6 months of the financial year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing attracts administrative fines up to EUR 2,000 (approximately USD 2,200); repeated failure may result in court-ordered compliance and potential administrative strike-off after registry notification.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO data confirmation declaration (confirmation annuelle des bénéficiaires effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE) – Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Once per calendar year, during the calendar month corresponding to the anniversary of the initial RBE registration; entities registered before 1 March 2019 must confirm by 31 March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late confirmation penalty up to EUR 125 (approximately USD 135); serious or repeated breaches may expose legal representatives to fines up to EUR 500 and criminal sanctions under the Luxembourg UBO Law.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax (IRC) and municipal business tax (ICC) annual return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (Luxembourg direct tax authority)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For calendar-year taxpayers: initial deadline is 31 May of the year following the financial year-end; electronic filing before 31 May extends the filing deadline to 31 December
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing and late payment interest accrues at 0.6% per month on outstanding taxes; additional penalties range from EUR 50 to EUR 3,000, with possible tax assessments on an estimated basis.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Net wealth tax (impôt sur la fortune, IFT) annual return and minimum net wealth tax declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (accepted via the same corporate tax filing channel)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Fiscal year, due together with the corporate income tax return; same deadline rules apply (31 May, extended to 31 December upon valid electronic filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing or omission triggers interest at 0.6% per month on the net wealth tax due, plus fines up to EUR 3,000; the minimum net wealth tax remains payable regardless of profits.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit by a réviseur d'entreprises agréé is required if the SARL exceeds at least two of the following criteria: balance sheet total above EUR 4.4 million, annual net turnover above EUR 8.8 million, or average workforce above 50 employees; audit is also required for public-interest entities or where consolidated/regulatory rules impose it.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP pursuant to the Law of 19 December 2002 on accounting and annual accounts (implementing EU Accounting Directive 2013/34/EU); EU-endorsed IFRS is required for consolidated accounts and may be voluntarily applied for individual statutory accounts; financial statements are denominated in euro.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Each SARL must retain and confirm current UBO data in the RBE annually, within one month of the registration anniversary or by 31 March for earlier registrations; any change in shareholding, control, or beneficial ownership must be declared within 30 days of that change.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 950 – 2,950 (EUR 800 – 2,500, typical annual registered office/domiciliation agent fees)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000 – 12,000 (EUR 2,500 – 10,000, typical annual certified audit fee for an animation/VFX SARL)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% (combined corporate income tax, solidarity surcharge, and Luxembourg-City municipal business tax)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 80% exemption for qualifying intellectual-property income under the Luxembourg IP box; notional interest deduction on new cash equity; participation exemption on qualifying dividends and capital gains

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulaire 970 (Corporate Income Tax Return) filed via MyGuichet.lu electronic filing (eCDF)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due on or before the last day of the sixth month following the fiscal year-end; automatic extension to 30 September for e-filing when the fiscal year ends on 31 December

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income or deficit for the fiscal year
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: File as a Luxembourg resident company; non-residents with a Luxembourg permanent establishment report attributable net income in this box
Only Luxembourg-sourced losses may be carried forward; gains/losses of a Luxembourg PE must be separately accounted for

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Adjustments pursuant to Article 56bis LIR (transfer-pricing adjustments)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents must disclose intercompany pricing with Luxembourg PEs and related parties, including methods used

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Withholding tax credits, prepayments, and tax reliefs
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report Luxembourg withholding taxes suffered and prepayments made by or on behalf of the foreign corporation

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Attachments: tax residence certificate, financial statements, TP documentation, group chart
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporations must annex the tax residence certificate and audited statutory accounts of the Luxembourg PE

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a 10% surcharge on the tax due, daily late-payment interest, administrative fines up to EUR 25,000, and a potential tax assessment on a discretionary basis

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke treaty relief, the shareholder must provide a tax residence certificate (TRC) to the paying Luxembourg SARL before the dividend distribution; the payer then applies the reduced treaty rate or the Luxembourg tax administration issues a withholding-tax release (visa pour décharge). A domestic refund claim may be filed if excess WHT is withheld.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory: 0% on both interest and royalties paid to non-residents; treaty rates generally 0%–5% for interest and royalties under OECD-pattern treaties, with most treaties preserving 0% on interest and a 2.5%–5% rate on royalties

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 50,000,000 consolidated group turnover to obligatory preparation of Local File and Master File; CbCR threshold EUR 750,000,000
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not legislate a discrete ESR code but applies the EU ATAD substance-over-form, the OECD nexus approach, and the SOPARFI substance expectations; companies must demonstrate real personnel, decision-making, invoicing, and risk-management capacity commensurate with their IP, finance, and animation-production functions

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentional understatement of taxable profit by bookkeeping manipulation, use of fictitious invoices, or omission of foreign-derived animation revenue from the Luxembourg return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fine up to EUR 25,000 or the amount of evaded tax (whichever is greater) and/or custodial sentence up to five years; immediate assessment of evaded corporate income tax with 100% penalty and interest
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false returns or orchestrate the concealment are jointly and severally liable for the underlying taxes; can face the same criminal penalties, travel bans, and debarment from managing Luxembourg companies

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a Luxembourg SARL as a letterbox entity with no staff, discretionary board powers, or substantive 3D animation production activity, used solely to access the participation exemption or DTA relief
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Disallowance of the participation exemption and treaty benefits; recharacterization of transactions under Article 56ter LIR; retroactive tax assessment plus 5% monthly late-payment interest and administrative fines
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be personally charged under the 'abuse of law' doctrine for the additional tax, have decisions voided, and be subject to professional debarment if they knowingly facilitated the artificial arrangement

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting third-party client payments (e.g., via Wise B2B or swift wire) without performing KYC/beneficial-ownership checks or filing a suspicious-transaction report; misrepresenting the final beneficial owner
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine up to EUR 1,000,000 or 10% of annual turnover for the SARL; suspension of operations; reporting to the Financial Intelligence Unit
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face criminal imprisonment up to five years, personal fines, and prohibition orders where money-laundering facilitation is established; the corporate veil is pierced for civil restitution to victims
